clues.title: Plate: short, white with turquoise top strip
text: Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal **turquoise strip **on the** top**. Rarely, the strip can have [other colours](https://goo.gl/maps/xCKZgTN28Dzp9W8w6).
Front plates are **not **required in Panama.
clues.summary: Short plates, usually white with a turquoise strip across the top (rarely another colour). Front plates are not required, so many cars show none at the front.

clues.title: Google car: big white pickup, fully blurred
text: Panama was covered by a large white pickup truck that is usually **entirely blurred**. An antenna is occasionally visible.

NOTE: The [Costa Rican](https://maps.app.goo.gl/468aLVF3daz21MRLA) truck is usually unblurred. The car used in [Ecuador](https://maps.app.goo.gl/dSweUPGTkgTasq9B7) has neither an antenna nor a white metal railing.
clues.summary: A large white pickup truck, usually blurred out completely, with an antenna sometimes visible. Costa Rica's truck is usually not blurred; Ecuador's car has no antenna and no white metal railing.

differs.how: Costa Rican truck is usually unblurred
Ecuadorian car has no antenna or white railing

clues.title: Landscape: tropical hills, palms, dry fields
text: Panama is a tropical country with a lot of hills. You will find a lot of palms and other tropical plants along with drier rolling hills and fields.
clues.summary: A tropical country with lots of hills, many palms and tropical plants, plus drier rolling hills and fields.

clues.title: Fence: living tree posts, wooden posts
text: Most roads are paralleled by fences that are partly or fully made out of small trees. The rest of the fence posts are also almost always wooden.
clues.summary: Most roads have fences that are partly or fully made from small living trees. The remaining posts are almost always wood.

clues.title: Houses: painted concrete, red roofs, barred windows
text: Panamanian architecture often reflects **Spanish colonial influences**, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing. The most common type of building has **painted concrete** or sometimes brick** **walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof. Many** **windows have bars on them for security.
clues.summary: Colourful painted concrete (sometimes brick) houses with red metal sheet or tile roofs, some ornate detail, and security bars on many windows.

clues.title: Road lines: white edge lines, yellow centre
text: Panama features a diverse set of road lines, but the most common combination is [solid outer white with an inner yellow line](https://goo.gl/maps/KAGUqGk3zVKLnNXH8). However, those are not unique to Panama. Within Latin America, solid outer white lines with no middle line are almost unique to Panama.
clues.summary: Many styles, but most common is a solid white edge line with a yellow centre line, which is not unique. Solid white edge lines with no centre line are almost unique to it within Latin America.

clues.title: Pole: round concrete pole
text: Panama uses a wide variety of poles, but the most common type is a **round concrete pole**, with a varying amount of insulators. Poles can also be wooden or metallic. They often have [plates](https://goo.gl/maps/5u2MsQ5wAd6cLHTt7) attached to them. [Blue](https://goo.gl/maps/wCUF3vx7iUtNgZjAA), [white](https://goo.gl/maps/4wmrWMk22ZnZtY3x5), or [red](https://goo.gl/maps/4tDyan7Qz2WnrPsX9) numbers are commonly painted on them as well.
clues.summary: Many pole types, but round concrete poles with a varying number of insulators are most common. Wooden and metal ones exist. Plates with blue, white or red painted numbers are often attached.

clues.title: Taxi: yellow with chequerboard stripe
text: **Yellow **taxis with a **chequerboard patterned horizontal stripe** are a common sight in Panama. The licence plate will be drawn on the side, containing the city name and a [regional code](/panama#taxiplates).

images.caption: Yellow taxi with a chequerboard stripe; the circle zooms in on its plate

clues.summary: Yellow taxis with a chequerboard stripe along the side are common. The plate is painted on the side with the city name and a regional code.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign says ALTO, thick font
text: Panama uses the Spanish word “**ALTO**” on stop signs.

NOTE: [Mexico](https://goo.gl/maps/f1zLdwAo5VhYDhtC7), [Costa Rica](https://maps.app.goo.gl/K6pZqyNn2Hw52GXJ7) and [Guatemala](https://www.google.com/maps/@14.6255005,-90.5568668,3a,15y,74.14h,81.77t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1smSi97ivNOrtG5_baoEx9YQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) also use “ALTO”, but the font is thinner.
clues.summary: Stop signs say ALTO in a thick font. Mexico, Costa Rica and Guatemala also say ALTO but with thinner letters.

differs.how: Costa Rican ALTO letters are thinner

clues.title: Sign: red octagon with a realistic eye
text: Red octagonal signs with an oddly **realistic eye** are unique to Panama.
clues.summary: Red octagonal signs showing an oddly realistic eye. Unique here.

clues.title: Coverage: gaps on north coast and east
text: While Panama is quite well covered, there is barely any coverage on the north coast, or east of Panama City.
clues.summary: Coverage is good overall, but there is hardly any on the north coast or east of the capital.

clues.title: Phone numbers: first digit shows the region
text: The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama.
The numbers with a smaller font indicate potentially useful [regional two-digit codes](https://goo.gl/maps/fgoa9tJUxY5QL2C56).
NOTE: Only phone numbers with 7 digits are helpful, and any numbers starting with 5, 6, or 8 are useless as well.
clues.summary: The first digit of a 7-digit number points to a region, and smaller-font two-digit codes help too. Numbers starting with 5, 6 or 8 are useless.

clues.title: Plate: first digit of taxi or bus plate
text: The first digit of taxi and bus licence plates can be used to regionguess Panama.
NOTE: Cars travel, so they are not always reliable, especially outside of cities.
clues.summary: The first digit of taxi and bus plates points to a region. Cars travel, so it is unreliable, especially outside cities.

clues.title: Landscape: green tropical, tall grass, palms
text: **Green tropical landscapes** with palm trees and very tall grass** **are common around Colón and Panama City.
clues.summary: Around Colón and the capital: green tropical land with palms and very tall grass.

clues.title: Landscape: volcanic rocks and rock walls
text: **Volcanic rocks** that are either scattered on the ground, or built into **rock walls**, are common north of David.
clues.summary: North of David, volcanic rocks lie scattered or are built into rock walls.

clues.title: Landscape: very flat, open fields
text: The area around David is **very flat**, with lots of fairly **open fields**. Usually, [mountains](https://goo.gl/maps/MT8CapwfA7XwFeDw9) will be visible to the north and northeast.
clues.summary: Around David, the land is very flat with open fields, and mountains are usually visible to the north and northeast.

clues.title: Landscape: flat farmland, brown-orange soil
text: The region around Aguadulce is relatively **flat **and features a lot of agricultural fields along with very **brown or orange** soil.
clues.summary: Around Aguadulce, fairly flat with lots of crop fields and very brown or orange soil.

clues.title: Pole: tall vertical plate, black zip ties
text: The eastern provinces often have tall vertical plates that can be yellow or white. They are commonly attached to poles by black zip ties.

NOTE: Be careful not to mix them up with [these white vertical plates](https://goo.gl/maps/9UssGMTvSrtsLBN98), often attached by metallic zip ties. They are slightly wider than the eastern plates and always have 6 digits.

images.caption: Tall vertical plates tied to concrete poles with black zip ties

clues.summary: In the eastern provinces, poles often carry tall yellow or white vertical plates held by black zip ties. Don't confuse them with slightly wider white plates on metal zip ties, which always have 6 digits.

clues.title: Pole: horizontal plates in the west
text: Many poles in the western provinces will have **horizontal **plates attached to them. However, if one of these is accompanied by an [eastern vertical plate](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Fd541FefRusFDcE37), the eastern plate takes precedence.

images.caption: Horizontal plates and stickers on a concrete pole

clues.summary: Many poles in the western provinces have horizontal plates. If an eastern vertical plate is also there, the eastern one wins.

clues.title: Pole: thin yellow plate, black border
text: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border are most common in the Colón Province.

images.caption: A thin yellow plate with a black border on a concrete pole

clues.summary: Thin yellow plates, vertical or horizontal, with a visible black border, are most common in Colón Province.

clues.title: Landscape: wind turbines
text: Wind turbines can be seen [south](https://goo.gl/maps/NFm7beZBXA6frwMb7) and [north](https://goo.gl/maps/tbfJ4v7xXsSbRa4B8) of Penonome.
clues.summary: Wind turbines can be seen south and north of Penonomé.

clues.title: Landscape: very high road, dry mountains
text: The main covered road in the Ngäbe-Buglé province is very **high-altitude** and almost above the clouds. The surrounding mountains tend to be quite **dry**, and the altitude makes for many stunning views.
clues.summary: The main covered road in the Ngäbe-Buglé area is very high, almost above the clouds, with dry mountains around and big views.

clues.title: Landscape: green hills, cloudy all along
text: The road going to Changuinola features a lush and **green hilly landscape**. The weather is **cloudy **or overcast** **on the entire road.
clues.summary: The road to Changuinola runs through lush green hills with cloudy or overcast skies the whole way.

clues.title: Road: grainy divided concrete highway
text: Highway 9 going from Panama City north to Colón is a **divided concrete highway**. The road is visibly **grainy **and has a lot of **tar lines**. The landscape is lush and hilly.
clues.summary: Highway 9 from the capital north to Colón is a divided concrete road that looks grainy with many tar lines. The landscape is lush and hilly.

clues.title: Road: fresh tarmac, orange soil beside it
text: Most of Road 407 features a **freshly paved road**, with visibly **orange soil** on the sides of the road. The southern portion is [hilly](https://goo.gl/maps/jAhhHN6t4w56XvCM6), right before the road quality [deteriorates](https://goo.gl/maps/F59mLWj9TrUS9LXM8).
clues.summary: Most of Road 407 has freshly paved tarmac with visibly orange soil at the sides. The south is hilly, before the road quality drops.

clues.title: Houses: many white high-rises
text: Panama City can be recognised by the large number of **white high-rise buildings**.
clues.summary: The capital has a large number of white high-rise buildings.

clues.title: Houses: warehouses and rundown blocks
text: Colón features a lot of **warehouses **and **rundown multi-storey buildings**.
clues.summary: Colón has many warehouses and rundown multi-storey buildings.

clues.title: Plants: banana plantations
text: The region around Changuinola is filled with** banana plantations.**
clues.summary: The area around Changuinola is full of banana plantations.

clues.title: Coverage: sunset light, small southern road
text: **Sunset **coverage can be found in southern Panama on a small road south of Tonosi.
clues.summary: Sunset coverage appears in the south on a small road south of Tonosí.

clues.title: Landscape: pines, volcanic rock, dry grass
text: A mountainous** **landscape with **pine trees**, **volcanic rocks**, **dry grass**, and gravel roads can be found northeast of Volcán.
clues.summary: Northeast of Volcán: mountains with pine trees, volcanic rocks, dry grass and gravel roads.

clues.title: Pole: yellow pole socks
text: **Yellow pole socks** can be found near the Panama Canal, around the town of Gatún.

images.caption: Poles wrapped in yellow socks at the base

clues.summary: Yellow sleeves around poles are found near the Panama Canal, around Gatún.
